::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** Feb 28th 1885  
**From:** Elderfield, Otterbourne, Winchester.  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Blackburne](people/person_160.qmd)

Thank you for the sight of this. I have sent the review on to [Mr Shorthouse](people/person_1654.qmd).[^1] That [Glasgow paper](organizations/other_252.qmd) must have clever people belonging to it, for they always make notices to the purpose[^2] 

I have sent the proof to the printers, and hope it will get in this next April number.

It is very interesting to see what Mr Shorthouse likes as his interpretation  Artistically I think it was a great mistake of [Lewes](people/person_2160.qmd) to keep adverse reviews back- for if they are ever so foolish and provoking and reviews <u>are</u> much less useful than they were when I began, they shew one’s mannerisms and blunders.[^3] And as to their stinging, one gets hardened and cares very little. Is [your novel](other_books/otherbook_784.qmd) out? I have not heard of it, and I do not think you told me its name.[^4]

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: Gertrude Ireland Blackburne (1861-1951), journalist, novelist and contributor to *MP*.
[^2]: Joseph Henry Shorthouse (1834-1903).  Blackburne's review of his *The Little Schoolmaster Mark* (1884-5) appeared as 'A Conversation on Books'  *MP* 3s 9 (April 1885) 368-75.
[^3]: In a footnote  Blackburne cites 'a suggestive and appreciative review in a daily paper, (*Glasgow News*, Jan. 19,1885).'
[^4]: The fact that George Henry Lewes had carefully guarded George Eliot from the sight of unfavourable reviews had recently been revealed in  J. W. Cross, *George Eliot's Life* (1885).
[^5]: CMY's 1901 reference to Blackburne's  novel *Zig-Zag* (1885) suggests that she thought it dangerously liberal.
